# Copilot instructions for BenefitsOps Lab

You are helping improve a **synthetic employee benefits operations portfolio**, not a real employee-benefits system.

- All people, rates, coverage rules, country thresholds, employee tickets and financial impacts are fictional. Never imply affiliation with GitLab or an insurer.
- Separate India/INR and UK/GBP. Do not sum currencies or interpret illustrative rules as law.
- Benefits/insurance/claims decisions require human review and current authoritative plan documents.
- Never place health records, dependents, payroll data or personal identifiers in public code or AI prompts.
- Prefer readable, accessible HTML, responsive CSS, JavaScript ESM, pure business rules, and deterministic Node tests.
- Explain root cause, evidence, owner, and next step for every exception.
- Distinguish rule-based templates from optional LLM output. No automatic employee-facing messages.
- Update relevant READMEs and Mermaid flowcharts when introducing new workflows.

## Recommended Copilot Chat prompts

1. Review audit/core.mjs for duplicate-billing and enrollment effective-date edge cases. Propose tests using fabricated records only.
2. Write more unit tests for premium variance controls, unknown members and country/currency mismatches.
3. Suggest an optional business-hours SLA engine for service/core.mjs without changing existing elapsed-hour behavior.
4. Review the project README as a non-technical HR operations hiring manager: identify unclear language and missing privacy caveats.
5. Draft five mock interview questions testing reconciliation, employee inquiry escalation and responsible benefits communication.
